defects.mechanism: Registry.accept keyed operations only by operation_id. INV-301 and INV-302 both use op-41 for shop/O-17/BOOK with qty 2, but belong to north and south respectively; the second is an independent operation, not a replay. Identity must be (tenant, warehouse, operation_id), with immutable payload (order_id, sku, action, qty). INV-303 is the genuine north replay despite its different event_id. The fix scopes the identity and retains payload-conflict errors. ARC-CACHE-29 describes restart eviction in the retired r29 single-warehouse polling cache; r31 routes through the in-memory operation registry and never imports the legacy cache. ARC-LOG-29 and ARC-SNAPSHOT-29 concern that obsolete route and cannot override current r31 inputs.
defects.impact: The broken registry accepts one delivery and replays two, omitting the south hold and reporting only 2 reserved units. The missing hold blocks readiness even for the correct paid snapshot. Correct accounting accepts two operations, replays one, and holds 2 units in each warehouse for 4 reserved units.

defects.mechanism: select chose the snapshot with greatest delivered_at rather than greatest numeric source revision per (tenant, order_id). ORD-310 is paid revision 10 delivered at 09:00, whereas ORD-311 is pending revision 2 delivered at 09:05. Combined records ORD-301 and ORD-302 have the same reversal. The fix compares revision while retaining immutable status/captured_minor/lines conflict checks for every source revision. A newer pending snapshot remains valid. ARC-POLL-29 recommended latest poll time only because the retired r29 polling route lacked source revisions; current r31 source-snapshot-v3 supplies them. ARC-LOG-29 and ARC-SNAPSHOT-29 describe the old bridge, not the current feed.
defects.impact: The delayed older snapshot overwrites paid revision 10 with pending revision 2, making the order unready. In the joined replay this also rejects all refund deliveries as order_not_refundable, masking the independent refund identity defect. Selecting revision 10 restores paid eligibility; readiness additionally requires the inventory fix.

defects.mechanism: Ledger.accept used (tenant, provider, attempt_id), treating a new delivery attempt as a new refund. REF-321 and REF-322 are both shop/atlas/R-17 for O-17, amount 400, with different attempts. Identity must be (tenant, provider, refund_id), with immutable payload (order_id, amount_minor); order_id is not an identity component. The fix changes the tuple only, preserving registration before eligibility and capture checks so retries of rejected logical refunds also remain replays. ARC-MONEY-29 concerns decimal import rounding, while these r31 settled deliveries contain positive integer minor amounts. ARC-LOG-29 and ARC-SNAPSHOT-29 refer to the retired r29 import/bridge and cannot explain or supersede current records.
defects.impact: The isolated broken refund replay counts R-17 twice, spends 800 of the 1000 capture, and wrongly rejects distinct R-18 (REF-323, amount 500) as exceeds_capture. Correct accounting accepts R-17 once and R-18 once, replays REF-322, refunds 900 with no rejection, and leaves net 100. In the combined case this becomes visible after checkout eligibility is repaired.
